name: Modernist Studio Jewellery
summary: Small sculptures to wear, made by one artist at the bench. The materials are silver, brass wire and cut crystal, in abstract forms from modern art, with no regard for the value of the metal.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is a small sculpture. An artist makes it by hand from an idea about form, and the metal and the stones serve the idea.
design_principles: Begin with an abstract form from modern art: a mobile, a line, a plane or a biomorphic shape.
Make each piece by hand at the bench, and make no more than a few of each.
Use a modest metal such as sterling silver, brass or copper, and choose it for its form, not its value.
Cut a stone to a new design, for example a rock crystal with an optical line cut under the surface.
Bend and join wire into an open line, and let the empty space count as part of the design.
Keep the piece to one gesture and to two or three materials.
Leave the hand marks, and sign each piece with a mark.
Design the piece for the body: a pin that sits on the lapel, a cuff that follows the arm.
anti_patterns: Rows of equal diamonds in a platinum frame

silhouette.shape: A small abstract sculpture: an open brooch of wire, a cuff of bent silver, a pendant of rock crystal in a metal frame.
silhouette.line: Open and linear, with curves and straight lines used as in a drawing; asymmetrical.
silhouette.fit: Pinned on a plain lapel, hung on a short chain over a knit, worn on the wrist as a cuff.
silhouette.proportion: A brooch is 4 to 9 cm wide; a pendant is 3 to 8 cm tall; a cuff is 2 to 5 cm wide.
rules: Make the design as a drawing in line, with open space around it.
Mount a stone cut with an optical line in a plain bezel of silver.
Bend brass wire into a free line, and join the ends with a visible solder.
Place the piece off centre on the dress.

fabrics.rule: Use silver and brass wire for the line, and one cut stone or a piece of wood for the point of interest.

methods: stones cut to an artist's design
cold joins with a rivet or a pin
construction.closures: A simple pin with a catch, a spring clasp or a slide; a cuff with a spring fit.
construction.details: An off-centre form, a single cut stone, a visible hand mark and a maker's signature on the back.

surface.pattern: Open lines and planes; no repeat; a single accent of a polished stone.
surface.gloss: Low to medium: brushed or hammered silver at 20 to 50 GU, with a bright stone.
surface.wear: Silver tarnishes and softens; wire bends if it is pulled, so wear is part of the piece.

palette.strategy: Silver, brass and the clear colour of one stone, in a plain, quiet scheme.

processes: hand bending and soldering of wire
making.scale: One artist at a bench or a small studio; a few of each design, sold through a gallery or a museum shop.
making.signs: A hand mark, an off-centre design, a visible solder joint and a signed back.

pieces.form: Open brooch of bent silver wire
Pendant of rock crystal with an optical cut in a silver frame
Brushed silver cuff with an open end
Brass wire necklace in a free line
Ring with an off-centre cabochon in a plain bezel

positive: rock crystal with an optical cut

canonical_works.work: Pin of silver and optical-cut quartz

emotion.target_response: A quiet, thoughtful and curious feeling: the viewer reads a small idea in a line and a stone.

use_cases: a gallery or a museum shop line of art jewellery
a museum label for a studio piece
an image prompt for abstract hand-made jewels
avoid_when: the brief wants a rich, precious or formal look
the brief wants a repeat pattern or a set

modifiers.how: Cast the metal with a rough surface, enlarge the form and set uncut stones.
Add a flowing line, enamel and a natural subject, and keep the hand-made silver.

ornament_level.note: The form gives the interest; a plain cuff carries no ornament.
